top_temples.name: Laxminarayan Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the main entrance of Ujjayanta Palace, Agartala; built during the rule of Maharaja Birendra Kishore Manikya with royal financial contributions.

top_temples.name: Jagannath Temple, Agartala
top_temples.location_note: On the shore of Jagannath Dighi lake, Agartala; known for its intricate craftsmanship and vibrant festivals.

top_temples.name: Umamaheshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Opposite the Jagannath Temple, within the Ujjayanta Palace compound, Agartala.

top_temples.name: Chaturdasha Devata Temple (Fourteen Gods Temple)
top_temples.deity: Fourteen deities including Shiva, Durga, Vishnu, and Lakshmi
top_temples.location_note: Old Agartala, about 8 km from the city centre; built by the Manikya royal family (attributed variously to Govinda Manikya in the 1660s-70s and Krishna Manikya in 1761), most vibrant during the week-long Kharchi Puja festival.

top_temples.name: Maa Bhabatarini Temple, Agartala
top_temples.location_note: Agartala; a serene temple within the city.

top_temples.name: Longtharai Mandir
top_temples.location_note: About 30 km from Ambassa in the Longtharai valley, Dhalai district; a hillside temple serving as Ambassa's nearest major shrine.

top_temples.name: Kamaleswari Mandir
top_temples.location_note: About 35 km from Ambassa in the sub-divisional town of Kamalpur, Dhalai district; no closer well-documented temple was found within Ambassa town itself.

top_temples.name: Kalibari Temple, Dharmanagar
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Dighi (local pond) in Dharmanagar; the town's most prominent temple, especially active during Kali Puja.

top_temples.name: Hari Mandir, Dharmanagar
top_temples.location_note: Also on the banks of the Dighi in Dharmanagar, alongside the Kalibari Temple; one of the town's two most significant shrines.

top_temples.name: Lakhi Narayan Bari (Laxmi Narayan Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Kailashahar; one of the oldest temples in Tripura, with a mix of Hindu and Islamic architectural styles.

top_temples.name: Nutan Kalibari, Kailashahar
top_temples.location_note: Kailashahar; known for its architecture and intricate carvings.

top_temples.name: Bhabatarini Mandir, Kumarghat
top_temples.location_note: Kumarghat; founded 1981 on Shivachaturdashi, the town's main temple, busiest during Shiva Chaturdashi and Kali Puja.

top_temples.name: Shiva Temple, Bhabatarini Complex
top_temples.location_note: Within the same Bhabatarini Mandir complex in Kumarghat, alongside an Eco-Kid park and a Buddha idol.

top_temples.name: Mahamuni Temple, Sabroom
top_temples.location_note: Sabroom town; a Buddhist pagoda attracting pilgrims from India and abroad.

top_temples.name: Baishnab Pur Buddha Temple (Manubankul)
top_temples.location_note: Manubankul village, northeastern part of Sabroom subdivision; built under the leadership of Mathu Mog, hosts a week-long fair in March-April with Mahamuni and Owha festivals.

top_temples.name: Tripura Sundari Temple (Matabari)
top_temples.location_note: Udaipur's central shrine; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, gives the town its religious identity.

top_temples.name: Bhubaneshwari Temple, Udaipur
top_temples.location_note: On the eastern fringe of Udaipur town by the Gomati river; built by Maharaja Govinda Manikya (1660-1676), immortalized in Rabindranath Tagore's plays Rajarshi and Bisarjan.

top_temples.name: Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava
top_temples.location_note: Unakoti's central and largest rock-cut carving, about 8 km from Kailashahar; a colossal 7th-9th century Shaiva relief giving the site its name and identity.

top_temples.name: Ganesha-Durga-Nandi Rock Carvings, Unakoti
top_temples.location_note: Within the same Unakoti rock-cut complex, distinct from the central Shiva carving; includes a trio of Ganesha figures beside a waterfall, full-sized Durga reliefs, and giant Nandi bull images.
